text: Jackie is the sixth studio album by American singer Ciara, released on May 1, 2015, through Epic Records. After leaving her previous record label and releasing her self-titled fifth studio album in July 2013, Ciara took a hiatus to focus on her relationship with American rapper Future, which inspired her sixth album. In May 2014, Ciara gave birth to her first child and later called off her engagement to Future following public claims of infidelity. After the breakup, Ciara postponed the album's release and focused on motherhood while quietly recording new music. During the recording process, Ciara worked with long-time collaborators Harmony "H-Money" Samuels and Polow da Don, as well as less frequent producers Dr. Luke and Cirkut, and songwriter Diane Warren. The album is a predominantly pop and R&B record influenced by hip hop, dance-pop, house, electropop, trap, drum and bass, and 1990s R&B, with themes centered on love, betrayal, and motherhood. Named after her mother, the album features guest appearances by Pitbull and Missy Elliott. The lead single, "I Bet," was released on January 26, 2015, and debuted at number 96 on the US Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number 43. The second single, "Dance like We're Making Love," was released on April 28, 2015, and the album was promoted with a third single, "Give Me Love," which received a US urban contemporary impact date on June 9, 2015. The album peaked at number 17 on the US Billboard 200 with 25,000 album-equivalent units (19,900 in sales), the lowest first-week sales among her first six albums, and placed at number 13 on the Top Album Sales chart. Ciara embarked on the Jackie Tour in 2015, which included 19 US dates and later expanded to include Canada, though the tour was ultimately cancelled. The album received mixed reviews from critics, with Metacritic assigning it a score of 60 based on 8 reviews, indicating "mixed or average" reception. Some critics praised its production and variety, while others noted a lack of depth or personal insight. The album opens with "Jackie (B.M.F.)," a trap and drum and bass track about motherhood, followed by "That's How I'm Feelin'," a synth-driven song featuring Pitbull and Missy Elliott, and "Lullaby," a dance-friendly track with a metaphor about a new mom putting her partner to bed. Other tracks include "Dance like We're Making Love," a sultry midtempo pop song, "Stuck on You," a brash pop song, "Fly" with an '80s electro sample and Squarepusher chords, "I Bet" with lyrics on betrayal, "Give Me Love" as an EDM/house track, "Kiss & Tell" as a retro-soul bounce, "All Good" as a disco-lite pop song, "Only One" as a pop ballad, and "One Woman Army" as a dance-pop track with a robo-military march, all of which are lyrically about self-reliance. The album closes with "I Got You," a lullaby for Ciara's one-year-old son, Future Jr. Ciara stated that "Jackie" is her best body of work, reflecting her growth as an artist and mother, and that the album captures her emotional journey through vulnerability, ambition, and personal transformation.

The album achieved 900 in sales and had the lowest first-week sales among her first six albums; its sales ranked it at number 13 on the Top Album Sales chart. Credits are adapted from liner notes and iTunes.
